audit_findings.title: Taylor Adhesives creates an unmodeled perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $390 million purchase consideration; €500 million of 4.000% notes issued partly to finance the acquisition; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The historical OE anchor includes only the post-October 20, 2025 contribution and financing cost, while projected growth implicitly includes Taylor for full future periods.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 20, 2025, we completed our business acquisition of W.F. Taylor Holdings, Inc. ("Taylor Adhesives"), a Georgia-based flooring adhesives business, for the purchase price of approximately $390 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because the valuation leaves perimeter null despite a completed acquisition. Taylor can increase OE through acquired earnings but decrease it through maintenance investment, taxes, and acquisition-financing interest. First-half 2026 filings show acquisitions contributed approximately two percentage points to Materials Group sales growth, but do not isolate Taylor's owner earnings. The record therefore cannot establish whether the net effect is large enough to close the $9.46-per-share gap between the $165.60 bull value and the $175.06 market price.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year pro forma Taylor OE using acquisition-date revenue, operating profit, maintenance investment, taxes, and attributable financing interest; reconcile it to FY2025 OE and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Temporary incentive-compensation savings may inflate normalized earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily low recurring compensation expense can raise FY2025 OE and, through that observation, the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate an unfavorable impact to our operating income from normalization of the majority of our 2025 temporary cost savings, which was largely related to lower incentive compensation.
audit_findings.explanation: Management expressly identifies temporary 2025 savings and continues to forecast their normalization in 2026, so the underlying normalization issue is demonstrated. However, neither filing isolates the amount included in FY2025 earnings, and the $756.3 million trend anchor is already below the $775.7 million latest OE. The record cannot establish whether the remaining anchor distortion is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025-versus-normal incentive-compensation expense bridge, calculate the after-tax OE effect, normalize FY2025 only for the temporary saving, and rerun the log-trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Dutch pension transition may create an unrecognized senior cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uncompensated obligation would reduce future OE when paid or require a separate deduction in the equity bridge if it is not already accrued.
audit_findings.evidence: Our Dutch defined benefit plan includes a minimum guaranteed funding ratio that will have to be terminated as part of the transition, for which we will have to compensate the Dutch Pension Fund.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation to compensate the Dutch Pension Fund is disclosed, but its amount, payment timing, and accounting recognition are not. The broader non-U.S. plans had $732.5 million of assets, $680.2 million of projected obligations, and a $52.3 million net funded position at year-end 2025, but those aggregate figures neither measure nor bound this specific compensation. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Dutch transition actuarial estimate and payment schedule, trace any amount already included in pension liabilities or projected OE, and rerun the bridge or OE forecast for only the uncaptured portion.

audit_findings.title: Discrete 2025 tax benefits may remain in the owner-earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.6 million disclosed valuation-allowance benefit; favorable-ruling benefit unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax benefits increase FY2025 OE and can raise the fitted OE anchor; recurring consequences of the restructuring or interest deduction belong in normalized taxes.
audit_findings.evidence: Our 2025 provision for income taxes included (i) $15.4 million of net tax charge related to the tax on global intangible low-taxed income ("GILTI") of our foreign subsidiaries and the recognition of foreign withholding taxes on current year earnings, partially offset by the benefit from foreign-derived intangible income (“FDII”); (ii) $10.6 million of tax benefit from the release of valuation allowance as a result of completing a foreign restructuring transaction; and (iii) net tax benefit from a favorable ruling related to deductibility of interest expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The $10.6 million valuation-allowance release is a demonstrated discrete benefit, while the favorable-ruling benefit is disclosed but not quantified. Removing only the known $10.6 million from FY2025 OE would reduce the fitted anchor by approximately $3.7 million and the bull value by approximately $0.8 per share, versus the $9.46 gap to market. That known portion is not material, but the record cannot close the finding because the ruling benefit and its treatment in OE remain unknown.
audit_findings.action: Trace both benefits through the FY2025 OE calculation, quantify the favorable-ruling amount, distinguish one-time recognition from recurring tax effects, and rerun the anchor and scenarios after removing only discrete amounts.

audit_findings.title: Venture investments are not coherently matched between OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $132.3 million carrying value at 2026-06-30, equal to $1.71 per diluted share; filed 2024 and 2025 venture-and-other investment losses were $19.2 million and $23.3 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitting the venture assets understates the equity bridge; retaining associated non-operating losses in OE also depresses the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to the investments described above, we hold venture investments that had a total carrying value of approximately $58 million and $45 million as of December 31, 2025 and December 28, 2024, respectively, which was included in “Other assets” in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The zero-stakes bridge is demonstrably inconsistent with the filed $132.3 million carrying value. Nevertheless, adding the full carrying value and conservatively assuming the filed 2024 and 2025 losses were retained in OE would raise the recomputed trend anchor to approximately $769.5 million and the bull value to approximately $170.1 per share. That remains below the $175.06 market price; the base value would remain approximately $145.0 per share. The documented mismatch therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm year-by-year removal of venture gains and losses, add the corresponding investments net of associated liabilities to the bridge at an evidenced value, and document the corrected presentation in the next rerun.
